By the letter of H4 this is a rule breach; I rate it major and not blocker only because the same verdicts stand with their words in part 4.1 directly above.
findings.evidence: My fake run runB (candidate walk/v0.4 at 10 ms: both R2 rows pass; the seeds5042 record of R2/42 fails reading 2). Part 4.1 prints `shown [R2/42@10ms: not replicated; R2/43@10ms: replication not run yet]`. Part 4.2 prints for F25F9cl: `incomplete: 1; not attributed: 1; not read: a1_over: 1; not run: 12; shown: 1` (BAR_TABLES.md line 487 of outB). findings.fix:
At line 1298 tally the printed cell where it is a verdict word: `cell = v[rkey]; word = cell["text"] if cell["verdict"].startswith(("shown", "provisional")) else cell["verdict"]; tally[rkey][word] += 1`, so the candidate's line reads e.g. `shown [R2/42@10ms: not replicated; R2/43@10ms: replicated]: 1` (a control's reads `shown [a control is not replicated]`). Print the tally as a list (`
`-joined `word = n`) instead of `word: n; ...`. Add a test: no tally key of a candidate line equals `shown`, `provisional`, `shown but for A1` or `provisional but for A1`.

findings.where: replication_word, lines 863-873 (line 871 passes in_order=True for every cell); used by verdict_of line 902 and replication_table line 1355
findings.problem: For a passing candidate record whose replication is in no unit of the registered order, the replication word depends on whether some unrelated unit of the task was cut. The chain (stage2/runs/2026-11-15-75cm/run_75cm.sh lines 134, 166-167; H6) replicates task 4's `@rest` at 10, 0, 4, 6 ms but never tier 6's reported ladders at 10 ms (`@ladders`), and never task 3's tier 9 (speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms). For such a record the tables print `replication not run yet` for ever when the task has no cut (not one of H4's three words), and `replication cut by the pre-registered order` as soon as any other unit of the task is cut, although no unit holding that replication exists or was cut. Task 4's last tier is the likeliest to be cut, so the real tables will probably hit the second case. H4 (every pass is replicated "in H6's order") and H6 (no replication of those tiers) disagree; the word needs the lead's ruling.
findings.evidence: runB (task 4 without a cut; F25F9cl `turn/t90_0.5_left` at 10 ms passes under both rows): `shown [R2/42@10ms: replication not run yet; R2/43@10ms: replication not run yet]`. runC (same records; budget.json gains a cut unit `T4.7-F25F9cl-0ms-seeds5042` and the started unit `T4.6-F25F9cl-10ms`): the same cell prints `shown [R2/42@10ms: replication cut by the pre-registered order; R2/43@10ms: replication cut by the pre-registered order]`.
findings.fix: Add the replication units of H6 as data, e.g. `REPLICATED = {(key, ms) for key in _group("@walk") for ms in WALK_DELAYS} | {(key, ms) for key in _group("@speed-ladder") for ms in (10, 0)} | {(k, ms) for s, k, ms in PR_ROWS if s == "F25F9cl"} | {(key, ms) for key in _group("@rest") for ms in REST_DELAYS}`, and at line 871 pass `in_order=(key, bar.delay_ms(row)) in REPLICATED` (explicit cut paths still win). For a passing record outside that set return one fixed phrase the lead rules (for instance "replication cut by the pre-registered order" always, with a table note that H6 holds no replication of task 4's tier 6 and task 3's tier 9), never a word that changes with an unrelated cut. Test both ledgers.

verdict: No blocker found; three majors and ten minors. The tables regenerate byte for byte in every run I made (my two fake directories, the runner's smoke directory, three hash seeds, a copied run directory, dest equal to the run directory), and my regeneration of the builder's smoke output is identical to the files the builder left. The JPS section 2.3 constants equal the file's cells (header and 10 rows of 7 cells, 0 differences), and its numbers stand only in the columns headed "JPS's claim". Measured values, limits and definitions sit in separate columns. On my fake records the words follow H1 to H3: 17 of 20 passes and 16 does not, `provisional` with one row, `shown` only with both rows at 10 ms, `passes at 4 ms` at a reported delay, `not read: a1_over`, `incomplete` for an episode that failed to run, `not run` with its reason, and `cut by the pre-registered order` from the ledger. Replication stands beside the headline and is never summed. The three majors are places where a study rule's wording is not met: the at-a-glance tally prints the candidate's `shown` and `provisional` counts without replication words (H4); the replication word for passes whose replication is in no unit of the order changes with an unrelated cut (H4 against H6, needs the lead's ruling); and the plan's list "Not run in this round, by name" is mostly absent from the tables. Not verified: records of R2 rows, attribution records and a ledger written by the real runner. None exists yet (rule R4), so those paths rest on records and a budget.json I wrote by hand to bar.py's schema; the 16 real records available are R0 smoke records on a fixture set. The worktree was left untouched (`git status --porcelain` empty throughout); all scratch files are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mesozoic-labs/2dca1c00-13f3-5853-acf6-8c3e3e04feb6/scratchpad/review_wp_t_tables/.
